behavior_anomalies.quote: t21 clinical-staff did release-one-completed-ventilator: flu-patients.patient_group.on_ventilators 1->0; flu-patients.patient_group.recovering 0->1; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.available_count 20->21; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.in_use_count 1->0

Meanwhile, patients requiring ventilation continue increasing, reaching 26 by t34, without corresponding allocation, deterioration-to-death, or other consequence for this unmet demand.

behavior_anomalies.quote:
t27 process receive-in-transit-ventilator: medical-supplier.supplier.orders_in_transit 1->0; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.available_count 23->24; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.operational_count 27->28; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.total_count 27->28
t27 process progress-unventilated-waiting-patients: flu-patients.patient_group.dead 26->27; flu-patients.patient_group.patient_count 6->5; flu-patients.patient_group.waiting_for_ventilation 1->0
behavior_anomalies.why: The run has 24 available ventilators while patients continue to wait for ventilation and die. Across the log, available_count only increases as ventilators arrive; no allocation or use ever reduces it, even though patients repeatedly require ventilation. This makes the ventilator dynamics physically implausible.

behavior_anomalies.quote:
t6 process receive-in-transit-ventilator: medical-supplier.supplier.orders_in_transit 2->1; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.available_count 9->10; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.operational_count 10->11; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.total_count 10->11

behavior_anomalies.why: A waiting patient dies immediately after the hospital has 10 available ventilators. The log shows no allocation or utilization of those available ventilators, which is physically and socially implausible for a hospital deciding who gets ventilated.

behavior_anomalies.quote:
t28 process receive-in-transit-ventilator: medical-supplier.supplier.orders_in_transit 2->1; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.available_count 32->33; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.operational_count 32->33; ventilator-inventory.ventilator_inventory.total_count 32->33

behavior_anomalies.why: The committee continues placing orders despite 33 available ventilators, zero ventilators in use since t9, and only 22 patients requiring ventilation at t28. The repeated ordering is disconnected from allocation or demand and drives inventory upward without an apparent operational cause.

This is followed by repeated deaths of waiting patients while inventory continues to grow.

rule advance-one-hospital-day can never be offered: its actor selector {'categories': ['time', 'ongoing-process'], 'components': []} matches only entities that cannot act; the actor must be an entity in category 'actor' (put the object it uses in participants).
rule place-one-ventilator-order creates ventilator_inventory.orders_placed from nothing; elsewhere that quantity only moves between things, so it must come from a stock that loses it.
